reasoning: Hard gates fail: kelvin_ok=false, 3 unconnected ratlines (both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO plus 1 unidentified net per the Rule-12 named/count mismatch — unconnected=3 but only 2 nets named in failing_reasons), DRC=34. The most significant observation this round: the directed stub summary nets=['/CAN_H','/I2C_SCL','/I2C_SDA'] contains zero /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO names, despite cable-1's Kelvin pair belonging in kelvin_stub_priority (Rule 11 requires adding both nets after any round they appear in failing_reasons). Three existing rules should independently have halted this dispatch before FR ran: (1) Rule 11 — any kelvin_stub_priority net absent from both the stub nets list and compile_failures must be treated as a compile_failure and dispatch aborted; /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO meet this condition exactly. (2) Rule 8 — absorbed=6 with post-absorption stub nets containing zero /SENSEC* names satisfies absorber_kelvin_purge_detected (absorbed>=1 AND no Kelvin nets survive absorption); if those nets were injected before absorption, a permanent halt flag should have been set. (3) Rule 13 — trimmed_spurs=1 requires verification that no Kelvin-exclusion-list net was trimmed; if /SENSEC1_HI or /SENSEC1_LO was the trimmed stub, trimmer_exclusion_broken=True applies. All three halt conditions appear to have been unenforced. The new manager rule addresses a gap not covered by any of the 23 existing rules: per-cable consecutive Kelvin failure stall detection that fires independently of stub-injection and abort-enforcement machinery — so that even if Rules 8/11/13 are bypassed (as evidently happened here), a bounded-consecutive-failure circuit breaker forces human review before the loop spins indefinitely on a structurally unroutable cable. For the scorer penalty: raising drc from 50 to 75 adds 850 objective points of DRC-avoidance pressure (34 violations × 25 delta), nudging FR toward less-congested routing corridors that may also reduce the obstruction preventing /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO from being placed, without diluting the dominant kelvin_unrouted=1000 and gate_fail=1000 signals.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Current DRC=34 at weight 50 contributes 1700 to the objective; raising to 75 increases DRC-avoidance incentive by 850 points (34×25). Routing congestion that produces 34 clearance/annular violations in a solved candidate is the same congestion that traps the Kelvin pair; a stronger DRC penalty pushes FR to widen routing corridors, which is the precondition for routing the stranded /SENSEC1 pair. Weight 75 is a 1.5× step — meaningful but not large enough to swamp kelvin_unrouted (1000) or gate_fail (1000), preserving priority ordering.

manager_rule: When the same cable index N — determined each round by parsing all /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO net names from failing_reasons entries that contain 'has unconnected ratlines' — appears with at least one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO failing in five or more consecutive rounds, the manager MUST immediately emit a 'kelvin_structural_stall' event and halt all FR dispatch, regardless of whether any Rule-8, Rule-11, or Rule-13 halt fired or was bypassed during any of those five rounds. The halt payload MUST include: (a) cable index N and the exact consecutive-failure round numbers; (b) the stub coordinates most recently derived from the board netlist for /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO; (c) for each of the five consecutive rounds: whether those net names appeared in the final stub nets list, the absorbed count, the trimmed_spurs count, and whether Rule-11's abort condition was evaluated and what its result was; (d) all bake_hints keepout regions (net name, bounding box) whose bounding box intersects or lies within 2 mm of either stub endpoint; and (e) the full per-net unconnected list from the scoring artifacts for the most recent round, annotated by Kelvin vs non-Kelvin class. This halt is independent of and accumulates alongside absorber_exclusion_broken and trimmer_exclusion_broken flags; all three must be cleared before FR dispatch can resume. Human clearance requires: (1) revised stub coordinates or removal/shrinkage of the conflicting keepout, AND (2) explicit written authorization confirming a viable routing path for cable N's Kelvin pair exists in the current board state.
